title: Report export check tool (part A of M0-T195): one new standard-library Python file, tools/report_export_check.py, and its self-test, tools/test_report_export_check.py, that check a printed report bundle for claims against drawings, cross-page consistency, schedule and allocation reconciliation, separate measurement bases, missing versus zero, page numbering, bookmarks, links, repeated table headers, clipping, global shrink and website/PDF agreement; red on the audited contradictions and on the shrunk print, green on a consistent case. No product code, record or CI file changed.
objective: Implement the rules of the design (A1-A5, B1-B10, C1-C7, D1-D9, E1-E4) in one new file under 600 lines of code (modularity WARN; split behind a facade if it grows past), Python 3.12 standard library only, calling only pdfinfo, pdftotext, pdftohtml and pdftoppm (poppler 24.02 on the build server) and, for A2, node apps/web/scripts/print-report-pdf.mjs; no package added, no network unless --fetch-links, no port, writes only under --out. Each rule returns PASS, FAIL, REVIEW or OWED with page, data-role and quoted text (at most 120 characters); a missing tool, file or unparseable input exits 2. The output never says verified or compliant and opens with: automated consistency check built by an AI agent; not professional verification. Expected labels come from docs/design/presentation-tokens.json, wording rules from the contract at the tested head, benchmark values from docs/reference-cases/R6B/cases/, the footprint and section roles from --roles; nothing from the product’s own constants.
business_reason: Passing tests did not catch the audited contradictions (outside audit 2026-10-15 section 10); the final export (M0-T195) and every later print need a repeatable output-level check that is shown to catch them.

acceptance_scenarios.given: a synthetic consistent bundle (footprint drawn and claimed, zones in proportion, schedule reconciled, bases labelled, one fingerprint)

report.html and report.pdf of 8fbf701b (the audited head) made with TestClient POST /api/v1/properties/4073340070/report, benchmark_provider(with_zoning_lot=True, street_on=True) and recorded_pack_provider(benchmark_215_16_northern_window), printed by print-report-pdf.mjs, no port, under the heavy lock
acceptance_scenarios.then: B1 FAIL (‘Shown on the site plan’, no footprint drawn) and B5 FAIL (zones claimed, none drawn); the same made at e026a391 gives no B1 or B5 FAIL and reports B3 and B7 OWED

acceptance_scenarios.given: main 86a450d4’s prints (outside git, sha256 pinned in the test)
acceptance_scenarios.then: report-with-commit-8-pages.pdf fails D7 (headline 25, title 19 against 30 and 22); report.pdf fails A1 (‘Code commit: unknown’) and D2 lists the four run-together bookmarks and page 4’s missing title bookmark

acceptance_scenarios.given: one-change mutations of the S1 bundle
acceptance_scenarios.then: a zone width changed fails B5/C2; ‘35.31 ft, city map outline’ changed to ‘printed tax map’ fails C4; an inserted 34.33 fails C4; a null value rendered ‘0’ fails C5; ‘NaN’ in text fails C5; the legitimate zero passes
it equals run_identity.document_fingerprint (the one test importing app, PYTHONPATH=services/api); the exclusion list is read from run_identity.py text at the tested head; a mismatch fails A4

acceptance_scenarios.given: a missing poppler tool, a missing bundle file, or a PDF with compressed object streams
acceptance_scenarios.then: exit 2, or REVIEW for the unreadable link annotations; never PASS

acceptance_scenarios.given: web dumps with horizontal scroll at 320 px, or no area illustration while the PDF draws zones, and before/after pictures
acceptance_scenarios.then: E1 FAIL; E3 FAIL or OWED; ‘unchanged’ only on equal digests
python3 tools/test_report_export_check.py passes; python -m ruff check on both files; python tools/modularity_check.py --check passes; no other path changed

risks: Real fixtures live outside git: the test reads them from REPORT_CHECK_FIXTURES and FAILS (never skips) when one is missing or its sha256 differs; the orchestrator keeps them in N12/check-fixtures/.
CI does not run tools tests unless ci.yml names them; G4 evidence is the qa-engineer’s own run at the frozen head (CI wiring is a later choice, not this task).
Builders never use ports 3000, 3001 or 8000; old-head prints come from git archive into /tmp and TestClient only.
path_notes: tools/** is lane C in docs/lanes/OWNERSHIP.yaml (no orphan); tools/report_export_check.py is not a governance path (project-control/config.json governance_paths), so task type backend. Test style follows tools/test_research_record_check.py (unittest, run as a script).
